info.name: Kioskium daemon API
info.description:
Start, stop and drive Kioskium browsers through the daemon (`kioskctl serve`), without a shell.

1. Start the daemon: `kioskctl serve`. It listens on `http://127.0.0.1:7000`; for a remote device, tunnel it: `ssh -L 7000:127.0.0.1:7000 user@device`.
2. Set the collection variables: `baseUrl`, and `name` for the browser to start (what the requests below call it). If the daemon runs with `--token`, put it in `token` (sent as `X-Kioskium-Token`; ignored otherwise).
3. Run **Instances / Start instance** first. Browser commands go to `/api/instances/{name}/<endpoint>`.

The whole collection can run in order (`npx newman run examples/kioskium-daemon.postman_collection.json --folder ...` or the Postman runner); leave out the **Events** folder, whose streams stay open. For a browser started on its own with `--control-port`, use kioskium.postman_collection.json instead.

Full reference: https://github.com/jerhemy/kioskium/blob/main/docs/API.md#8-daemon-start-browsers-over-rest-kioskctl-serve

item.name: Daemon
item.description: The daemon itself: no browser needed.

request.description: Is the daemon up? For monitors and probes: no token needed (this request sends none), and it answers only `ok`.

originalRequest.description: Is the daemon up? For monitors and probes: no token needed (this request sends none), and it answers only `ok`.

request.description: Version, pid and the names of the instances it manages. `daemon: true` tells it apart from a browser's own `/api/status`.

originalRequest.description: Version, pid and the names of the instances it manages. `daemon: true` tells it apart from a browser's own `/api/status`.

request.description: Every instance the daemon manages with its `state`: `starting`, `running`, `restarting`, `exited`, `failed` or `stopped`.

originalRequest.description: Every instance the daemon manages with its `state`: `starting`, `running`, `restarting`, `exited`, `failed` or `stopped`.

item.name: Instances
item.description: Start browsers and look at them. Run **Start instance** first: the later folders need a running browser.

request.description: Start a browser. `name` is what later requests call it (`/api/instances/{name}/...`). Optional: `appId` (its Wayland `--app-id`, which picks the output on Weston; default `kioskium`, and the name defaults to it), `url` (default: the idle loading screen), `args` (kiosk options as a list), `restart` (`on-failure` default, `always`, `no`), `wait` (seconds to wait for the page's control API, default 60). 409 if the name is already running. Each browser gets exactly these `args`: `--windowed` here keeps it in a normal window on a desktop; leave it out on a kiosk.

originalRequest.description: Start a browser. `name` is what later requests call it (`/api/instances/{name}/...`). Optional: `appId` (its Wayland `--app-id`, which picks the output on Weston; default `kioskium`, and the name defaults to it), `url` (default: the idle loading screen), `args` (kiosk options as a list), `restart` (`on-failure` default, `always`, `no`), `wait` (seconds to wait for the page's control API, default 60). 409 if the name is already running. Each browser gets exactly these `args`: `--windowed` here keeps it in a normal window on a desktop; leave it out on a kiosk.

exec: pm.test('state is running or starting', () => pm.expect(["running", "starting"]).to.include(pm.response.json().instance.state));

item.description: Forwarded to the browser: `/api/instances/{name}/<endpoint>` = that browser's `/api/<endpoint>`. Same bodies and replies as the control API collection.

request.description: The browser's `/api/health`: `ok` and the page `state` (`idle`, `connecting`, `loading`, `target`). The browser answers it on its UI thread, so an answer also means it is not hung. 409 while the instance is not running.

item.name: Events
item.description: Live Server-Sent Events streams. They stay open: press Cancel to stop, and leave them out of collection runs.

request.description: The daemon's own events: `started`, `ready`, `exited`, `restarting`, `stopped`, `failed`. A crashed browser shows up here even though its own stream ended with it. `: ping` every 15 s.

response.name: 200 OK

originalRequest.description: The daemon's own events: `started`, `ready`, `exited`, `restarting`, `stopped`, `failed`. A crashed browser shows up here even though its own stream ended with it. `: ping` every 15 s.

item.description: What failures look like. Each request expects an error status.

exec: pm.test('error says name must be a string', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error).to.include('must be strings'));
